description: A web developer exploring child-friendly astronomy education through an interactive Earth–Moon learning prototype. The concept, code and educational text were developed with OpenAI Codex assistance; feature direction included 3D visuals and Earth’s orbit.
summary: Space Made Simple is an AI-assisted educational web prototype for ages 7–11. Children explore Moon phases, rotate a 3D Sun–Earth–Moon model, watch Earth orbit the Sun and answer a short quiz with explanations. NASA educational resources inform the content. The current prototype teaches foundational astronomy; it does not yet implement the lunar or Martian outpost resource-balancing simulation requested by the selected challenge. The initial concept was AI-suggested, with participant-directed revisions including 3D visuals and Earth’s orbit.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

A child-friendly astronomy learning prototype with an eight-phase Moon explorer, interactive WebGL orbital models, a separate Earth-year timeline, and a three-question quiz with explanations. Camera controls support drag, arrow keys, tilt, zoom and reset. A grown-up section includes a torch-and-ball activity and NASA references.

HOW IT WORKS

Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas and WebGL, hosted publicly on Firebase Hosting. Procedural spheres illustrate the Sun, Earth and Moon; no NASA imagery or live datasets are redistributed. The Moon lesson models the approximately 29.5-day phase cycle. The separate Earth-year model uses approximately 365.25 days for Earth and 27.3 days for the Moon’s orbit relative to distant stars.

LIMITATIONS AND CHALLENGE FIT

This is foundational astronomy education, not a complete outpost management game. Life support, radiation shielding, power, food production and mission success/failure trade-offs are not implemented. Sizes, distances and tilt are exaggerated; orbits are simplified circles and eclipses are not simulated. Effectiveness has not been evaluated with children.

AI DISCLOSURE

The initial concept was suggested by OpenAI Codex, which generated and revised the code, text and procedural visual illustrations and assisted with checks and deployment. The participant directed feature revisions, including 3D visuals and Earth orbit. It must not be represented as an independently participant-originated concept. This disclosure also appears on the public website.

CHECKS

JavaScript syntax and desktop Chrome checks covered phase selection, 3D controls, Earth-year playback/pause and scrubbing, quiz feedback, scoring and reset. Mobile devices and assistive technology have not been formally tested.

RESOURCES

NASA educational references are listed below. Other tools: OpenAI Codex, Firebase Hosting, Google Fonts (DM Sans and Space Grotesk). No personal information is collected by the application.
